findings.claim: The diff extends the closure-feedback partial-write-failure contract from two stores to three (adding the new archive-report append) and adds a standalone 'named carve-out, not a precedent' bullet, but neither the two-to-three-store extension nor the new bullet is asserted by any of the required/forbidden string pins the same diff adds in engine/skills/actuals_instrumentation_contract_test.go, so this specific behavior change ships unproved even though the diff's own established practice in the very same file is to pin every other changed clause, several with explicit 'mutation-proven non-covering' rationale.
proof_refs: skills/inception-pipeline/SKILL.md:162 — 'On any partial-write failure (any of the three written, another not), report the inconsistency and STOP. Do not silently leave the stores out of sync.' replaces the removed two-store sentence but is not among the required substrings in the new R016_R017_R018_closure_feedback_anchor_prose, R021_required_drops_wall_clock, or R019_compute_time_deferral_rationale blocks.

skills/inception-pipeline/SKILL.md:177-178 — the updated 'Stop on partial closure writes' bullet and the wholly new 'The archive-report append is a named carve-out, not a precedent' bullet have no matching entry anywhere in the same test file's required-substring lists.

engine/skills/actuals_instrumentation_contract_test.go — sibling clauses in the same change ARE pinned with explicit rationale (the Execute-item-3 pin cites 'mutation-proven non-covering (verify round 3, W2)'; the checkpoint_count-boundary pin cites 'the bare pin survived deletion of this clause'), showing the authors already treat an unpinned changed clause in this exact file as a demonstrated regression vector, yet left these clauses in that category.

ORCHESTRATOR CONFIRMATION: a direct search of the shipped test file returns zero occurrences of 'any of the three written', 'not a precedent' and 'does not license editing', while the shipped skill file contains each exactly once — so the clauses ship and nothing asserts them.
